doc.title: Lanny Morgan interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999

title: Moving to Los Angeles and his mother's view of his career
summary: He moved west with his mother in 1944; she accepted his music because his City College study was serious.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Did your whole family come out to Los Angeles?

I came out with my mother in 1944. They told me we were going out for a vacation, knowing that we were moving out here, which was a dirty trick. My dad was on the road back there for a while, and that sort of really didn’t pan out because he joined us later but they separated soon after, eventually getting back together. So it was just my mother and I and her mother lived out here, and then eventually the whole clan moved out here, maybe about three or four years later.
How did she feel about your direction you were going in as far as being, in essence, following your father’s path. Is that the way she looked at it? I mean I’m assuming.

Well I think that — you know times were a little different then. I did do my share of drinking and whatever else goes with the business. But you know the depression I think was kind of a really a hard time for people and you not only had not an awful lot of work, but there was a lot of bootlegging and things like that. A lot of hoods were around and it was just really a wild time all over. And if you were in the entertainment business it was, I would imagine, it was really like some of the movies you see. It was really kind of difficult to deal with, if you were the spouse of somebody who was doing that and waiting for them to come home and sometimes they did and sometimes they didn’t. But my life was a little more structured and I always tried to keep that in mind, that I would really rather do something than fall off the ship in the middle of the ocean. And she saw it was serious too because when I went to City College I took not only the band but I was in the orchestra, I was in the woodwind, a couple of woodwind groups and I took harmony and counterpoint and arranging.
So it was a more serious schooled approach that maybe she could relate to.
